audit.why: Justice Punch (E, 11s) is his only engage — a dash knockup that interrupts Naafiri's dashes on hit. Shield of Durand (W, 18s) taunts at 275 range — held taunt is the button that eats a W dive. Hero's Entrance is 180s and cross-map. His P is an AoE auto-reset that cleaves the whole pack — the wind-up is the step-back cue.
audit.corrected: Numbers and the taunt/cleave interactions written into cooldowns and bullets.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E Eviscerate like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Galio Justice Punch: 11s at rank 1 — his dash knockup; he has no engage while it is down. - W taunt is 18s, R a 180s cross-map entrance. - Guard your E (11s) like a fifth summoner; the R (110s) goes to kill windows only.

edits.before: Q the bleed, Q the consume, E through with the pack piling — a six-body trade he answered with one rotation.
edits.after: His P cleave taxes every exchange — E's dash heal and packmate refresh pay the toll back on the way out.

edits.before: W-diving into held CC — the lock-on telegraphs, the dogs can't dodge, and the lane's one button answers everything.
edits.after: Without hounds your W dive is one body into a taunt-shield brawler — that is a stat check you lose alone.

edits.before: Galio wins by landing Justice Punch, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Galio wins by knocking your dash up with Justice Punch, taunting the pack with W, and cleaving all six bodies at once.
